description:
FILED s407 (Fable review, fable-answers-s406.md §5.2, DECIDED s407).  perl's
lexical features are inherited by eval STRING; PCL's eval-mode compile runs in
`pl2cl --server` on the bare eval text, so PPI parses it with NO features and a
`try {…} catch ($e) {…}` inside an eval string is one swallowing statement
(silent undef today; a die once #363 lands).  Same for `signatures` (PCL
tolerates both PPI shapes there, but only because it repairs after the fact).

DESIGN (do not re-derive): the eval SITE knows its features — PPI answers
`$element->presumed_features` for the eval statement's element (the same stack
the lexer keeps; `custom_feature_include_cb` from #360 feeds it).  Carry
{ features => [...] } in the server request NEXT TO eval_captures (Parser2's
eval lowering + pl2cl _run_server + the runtime's p-transpile-string), and in
_ppi_parse pass `feature_mods => { try => 'perl', … }` to PPI::Document->new
when the request carries them.  A capture-dependent EMISSION must key the eval
CACHE (s387 rule): the feature set joins the cache key.

BAR: perl-oracle rows: `use feature 'try'; eval q{ try/catch }` (value + $@),
`use v5.40; eval q{…try…}`, an eval WITHOUT the feature where `try` is a plain
sub (Try::Tiny shape) — must stay a call; two evals of the same text under
different feature scopes must not share a cache entry.  corpus-diff IDENTICAL
(file mode untouched); the sweep because the eval protocol changed (runtime
side).  Depends on #360's callback for the site's own detection of `use v5.40`.


DONE s408 (Opus 5), the design as ruled, with two corrections found by tracing.

FOUR LAYERS: ExprToCL emits (p-eval STR ALIST FEATURES) -- and keeps the
SHORTER forms byte-identical when there are no features, so nothing that has
neither lexicals nor features moves; the runtime p-eval takes the list, adds it
to the CACHE KEY, and passes it to p-transpile-string, which sends it as a
FIFTH protocol line; pl2cl reads it into eval_features; Parser2 turns it into
PPI's document-level feature_mods, which PPI::Lexer consults before the first
token.  The SITE's own answer is PPI ->presumed_features (exact and lexical: a
`no feature try` in an inner block turns it off there and back on after --
probed), computed ONCE per document and recorded against every enclosing
statement (one find + short parent walks; nothing per token, the #184 lesson).

TWO CORRECTIONS the design did not anticipate, both cost time, both worth
remembering:
  * `lex_home` IS THE PARSER2 OBJECT.  Publishing the per-statement value under
    the same key as Parser2's own per-document map made the reader see a
    hashref where it wanted an arrayref -- "Not an ARRAY reference", surfacing
    as a PARSE ERROR drop on EVERY eval statement.
  * THE HOOK IS _lower_block, NOT _lower_stmt.  The declaration paths
    (`my  = eval "..."` -- the commonest eval statement there is) never reach
    _lower_stmt, so the first version published nothing and the probe looked
    unchanged.  Traced, not guessed.

BAR, all met: perl-oracle guard rows in Pl/t/feature-pragma-01.t (S4) --
`use feature try` + eval, `use v5.40` + eval, an eval with NO feature where try
is a plain sub, and the CACHE rows (same text under two feature scopes, BOTH
orders, because a cache bug shows in only one).  corpus-diff 1 of 111:
signatures.t, and the difference is proven MECHANICALLY to be only the 530
feature arguments (strip them and the whitespace-normalized emissions are
byte-identical).  Gen v2-153 + three artifacts.  Sweep: the eval protocol
changed, so it was run.
subject: String-eval FEATURE inheritance: `use feature "try"` (and v5.40) in the enclosing scope must reach the eval'd text's PPI parse
